title: Starter-slab vs volume sensitivity & HC plan matrix (Apr 2027)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, working analysis comparing two go-to-market price constructs for a new low-commit offering ("Starter Slab") vs a traditional volume-commit tier ("Volume Discount") and the headcount / budget implications required to operate and support each band over a 12-month rollout. This is an internal playbook-style sheet (working numbers).

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Starter Slab: low barrier, high per-token price, limited SLA, minimal sales touch. Good for funnel expansion but worse unit margins at scale. Requires proportionally higher cost-ops and SRE to manage noisy small customers.
- Volume Discount: higher ARR commitment, lower per-token price, SLA-backed, sales-assisted. Better long-term unit economics but slower signups and heavier AM/CS investment initially.
- Recommendation: Run Starter Slab pilot Q1, gate conversion funnels to Volume Discount in Q3 using usage-based incentives. Prioritize instrumentation to measure churn by token intensity.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model cost (avg blended infra per 1k tokens): $0.28 (mix of g5/rtx A100 on demand, caching savings applied)
- Avg tokens per active small-customer month (Starter): 150k tokens/mo
- Avg tokens per mid-volume customer (Volume tier): 3,500k tokens/mo (3.5M)
- CAC estimates: Starter (self-serve) $120, Volume (sales-assisted) $4,800
- Conversion funnel Starter->Volume within 12 months: base case 8%, optimistic 15%, pessimistic 3%
- Support and SRE ratios scaled to active customers (see HC table)

Scenario pricing bands (proposed):
- Starter Slab: $0.065 per 1k tokens (billed monthly), no SLA, 30-day free trial credit $50
- Volume Silver: commit $5k/mo -> $0.035 per 1k tokens, SLA 99.9%
- Volume Gold: commit $25k/mo -> $0.022 per 1k tokens, dedicated capacity option

Scenario matrix (monthly unit numbers) -- header row columns separated by |
Scenario | Active customers (m) | Avg tokens / cust / mo | Revenue per cust / mo | Cost per cust / mo | Gross margin / cust / mo | Notes
Starter (base) | 1,200 | 150k | $9.75 | $42.00 | -$32.25 | many low touch accounts, high infra overhead per customer
Volume Silver (base) | 420 | 3,500k | $122.50 | $980.00 | -$857.50 | commit-based, heavy discount; need dedicated pooled capacity to hit cost
Volume Gold (base) | 45 | 7,500k | $165.00 | $2,100.00 | -$1,935.00 | economics only good with burst pooling + quantization

Note: above shows obvious negatives because per-cust costs in raw infra terms assume dedicated per-customer allocation for peak; we model pooling below (realistic blended cost per 1k tokens drops to $0.10 with pooling & batching).

Pooled-inference blended (optimized) assumptions:
- With pooling, batching, KV cache, and quantization mix, blended infra cost can be reduced to $0.10 per 1k tokens at scale. Use that as optimized baseline for final analysis.

Adjusted scenario matrix using pooling cost $0.10 per 1k tokens:
Scenario | Active customers | Avg tokens / cust / mo | Revenue per cust / mo | Cost per cust / mo | Gross margin / cust / mo
Starter (pooled) | 1,200 | 150k | $9.75 | $15.00 | -$5.25
Volume Silver (pooled) | 420 | 3,500k | $122.50 | $350.00 | -$227.50
Volume Gold (pooled) | 45 | 7,500k | $165.00 | $750.00 | -$585.00

Break-even analysis (per 1k tokens)
- Break-even price for Starter (given pooling + CAC & ops allocation to reach positive 12mo CLTV): $0.09 per 1k tokens (base case).
- Break-even price for Volume Silver (target unit margin >20%): $0.14 per 1k tokens unless we materially reduce CAC or increase commit levels.

Headcount plan (12 months) by quarter (FTEs incremental hires) -- columns: role | Q2-2027 | Q3-2027 | Q4-2027 | Q1-2028 | Notes
Role | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | Q1 | Rationale
SRE (inference ops) | 2 | 2 | 1 | 0 | build/run for pooling & SLA onboarding; frontload before Volume ramp
Platform Backend | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | implement metering, slab gating, autoscale rules
Cost-ops / Billing eng | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | billing reconciliation, meter accuracy, quota handling
CS/AM (for Volume) | 0 | 3 | 4 | 2 | handshake sales assisted accounts in Q3/Q4
Solutions Eng | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | POC work for large Volume conversions
Finance Analyst (pricing experiments) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | run pricing experiments and cohort CLTV analysis
Total hires | 4 | 10 | 8 | 4 | net ramp profile 

Approx incremental Opex by quarter (salaries + infra uplift for ramp) -- numbers are monthly run-rate at quarter midpoint, USD:
- Q2-2027 incremental monthly payroll: $55,000
- Q3-2027 incremental monthly payroll: $160,000 (sales hires drive jump)
- Q4-2027 incremental monthly payroll: $125,000
- Q1-2028 incremental monthly payroll: $65,000
- One-time infra + setup (pooling + telemetry): $210,000 (CapEx/Opex mix)

12-month P&L sensitivity (three cases):
Inputs varied: per-1k price, conversion Starter->Volume, pooling efficiency (cost per 1k tokens).
Case | Assumed price per 1k | Conv rate | pooled cost per 1k | Net contribution 12m (est, USD)
Base | $0.065 Starter / $0.035 Volume | 8% | $0.10 | -$1.2M (loss)
Optimistic | $0.09 Starter / $0.042 Volume | 15% | $0.085 | +$0.48M (profit)
Pessimistic | $0.05 Starter / $0.025 Volume | 3% | $0.12 | -$3.4M (loss)

Sensitivity takeaways: (working)
- Pooling efficiency is the single most sensitive variable. Each $0.01 reduction in pooled cost per 1k tokens improves EBITDA by ~$320k annually in our modeled mix.
- Conversion Starter->Volume is the second most important lever; improving conversion by 5ppt shifts the 12m contribution by roughly +$600k.
- CAC dilution for Starter matters only if churn is high; track 90-day active retention.

Operational guardrails & triggers:
- If pooled unit cost > $0.12 per 1k after Q3 pilot -> pause Starter expansion and shift marketing to Volume signups.
- If 90-day retention < 28% for Starter cohort -> increase trial friction (shorter free credits) and re-evaluate funnel incentives.
- If conversion rate > 12% by month 9 -> accelerate CS hires and prioritize dedicated capacity plans for Gold band customers.

Open questions / TODOs (immediate):
- Verify blended infra cost benchmarking with infra team: ask SRE to run 7-day load test with Starter-style distribution (JIRA-FF-731).
- Run at least two A/B pricing experiments for Starter price per 1k tokens (0.05, 0.065, 0.09) with cohort tracking (linked to experiment tag in product).
- Compute detailed per-route token mix (context length distribution) for early customers to refine caching assumptions.
- Align legal on trial credit T&Cs and refunds for Starter; potential fraud vector if credits abused.

Appendix: quick cohort math (starter cohort example)
- 1,000 Starter signups month 1 -> 35% active after trial -> 350 active -> median monthly tokens 150k -> gross monthly infra cost per cohort = 350 * 150k/1000 * $0.10 = $5,250; revenue = 350 * $9.75 = $3,412 -> immediate negative; must rely on conversion + expansion to reach positive LTV.

Notes and references:
- This is a working sheet meant for discussion. Numbers are intentionally conservative on revenue and optimistic on pooling efficiency in the optimistic case.
- Related docs: change-control for tier gating (confluence PRJ-392), staffing request form for Q3 hires (HR req ID: HR-2027-062).
